findings.summary: Asset pricing models formalize principles for valuing equities and debt instruments. Equilibrium pricing models, such as CAPM and multi-factor models, determine prices through market supply and demand, incorporating macroeconomic variables and investor preferences to reflect risk. Risk-neutral or rational pricing models value derivatives and fixed-income instruments by ensuring no arbitrage opportunities exist relative to fundamental securities, often using stochastic processes and state prices to derive unique risk-adjusted rates.

mechanisms.title: Equilibrium Pricing via Market Forces
mechanisms.explanation: Under general equilibrium theory, asset prices are set where supply equals demand, incorporating macroeconomic variables and investor preferences to reflect systematic risk. Models like CAPM and multi-factor models emerge from modern portfolio theory and use market-wide factors to price assets.

mechanisms.title: Rational / Risk-Neutral Pricing via Arbitrage-Free Conditions
mechanisms.explanation: Rational pricing calculates derivative and fixed-income prices so they are arbitrage-free relative to fundamental securities. This approach uses stochastic processes and state prices to derive a unique risk price for each asset, often assuming log-normal processes or incorporating mean reversion and stochastic volatility.

unknowns: How individual investor preferences are aggregated into market-clearing prices in large-dimension general equilibrium models
The exact calibration methods for stochastic process parameters in specific derivative pricing models
Whether state price densities can be uniquely recovered from observed market prices in all market conditions
The computational complexity of implementing multi-curve yield frameworks for complex interest rate derivatives
